corrections.was: milestone 2h: `32 unit record(s) exist and every unit pass of the frame and of the fixed step ticked 0 of them`
corrections.is: the world walk 00904bf0 and the motion virtual 00825f20 now run over the created units; what still ticks nothing is every pass that reads the world object itself, because construct_world 004de610 is a load record
corrections.evidence: the executable owns the chain header 009037f0 allocates at world+4h, which is the only thing 00904bf0 reads from the world (00904bf4 loads the field, 00904bf7 dereferences it again)

corrections.was: the packet brief: `hide the front-end frame pages once the mission state is entered if the state machine's screen sets say they are gone`
corrections.is: they are not gone. The mission load's own `select_front_end_layout` row is 00518250(3, 0), a non-committing call: src/title_init.cpp's reconstruction releases the other sets' handles and records the set only when commit is set (00518272, 0051864a), so FE_frame and FE_frame_title stay loaded through the mission
corrections.evidence: include/bsp/mission_scene_load.hpp `select_front_end_layout` comment, src/title_init.cpp select_front_end_frame_set, and the xref of 00518250 from 004e04ee in BSP_Game_LoadMissionScene

run.reason: Direct3D 9 reports zero adapters in this session, so the executable cannot create its device and exits before the window: the run log ends at `startup failed: Renderer adapter identification failed` with device_hr=0x80004005. The user's Windows session (id 1) is disconnected; a standalone probe over Direct3DCreate9 reports `adapter count = 0`, and the executable built from main before this packet fails identically, so the cause is the session and not this packet.
